title: Perceived burden and relief of caregivers through the use of modern, innovative, and needs-based assistive devices in the care of those in need of assistance.
summary:
Caring for people is currently facing major challenges, such as a shortage of skilled workers and an increasingly aging population. This project investigates how modern, innovative assistive devices and wearable technologies can improve everyday care practices. The aim is to determine whether and how these technologies can relieve caregivers in their daily work. Various modern solutions are being used, including intelligent beds that can measure weight or assist with repositioning, sensors and wearables such as smartwatches that detect falls or monitor vital signs like heart rate, as well as digital support tools like voice control for documentation or VR headsets to help activate and engage care recipients.

Caregivers and people in need of care are participating in the study. To allow for comparison, there are two groups: the technology group, in which new assistive devices are specifically selected, training is provided, and they are used in everyday care over a period of 12 months, and the comparison group, in which care is provided as usual using traditional aids. The main focus of the study is on how the workload of caregivers changes. In addition, it examines how user-friendly the technology is, whether it is accepted by all participants, and whether it improves the independence of those receiving care.

The results are intended to help improve care processes in the future. Participants contribute to the development of more practical assistive technologies and to the long-term improvement of working conditions in the care sector.
conditions: The study will include caregivers regardless of their health status, as well as individuals with unspecified care needs.

interventions.name: The study involves both caregivers and care recipients using contemporary assistive devices and wearables. The first study arm consists of caregivers and care recipients for whom this technology is being deployed or implemented.

The study involves caregivers and care recipients using contemporary assistive devices and wearables. The second study arm consists of caregivers and care recipients who do not use this technology. This group serves as the control group, performing care activities without any changes.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
For caregivers: Professional caregiving
For those in need of care: Care needs
Exclusion criteria:
Limited ability to understand participant information, informed consent, or the study protocols
